description.narrative: The main outcomes of the Project stem from an increase in the supply of sustainable electricity in Romania at a competitive tariff while contributing to a reduction of [ca. 368,000 tons of] CO2 emissions [annually]. Moreover, the Project will increase Romanias resilience through the diversification of its energy mix, where 56% of its generation capacity comes from fossil fuels. The Project is also expected to have demonstration effects by showcasing private-sector financing as an alternative to financing utility-scale renewable energy projects. Romanias energy sector is still dominated by state-owned companies, supplying more than 60% of power generation. The combination of merchant sales and local and cross-border commercial power purchase agreements (cPPAs) with corporate off-takers is expected to facilitate the use of cPPAs in the country to support scaling up private investments in renewables in Romania.

The project comprises of the development, design, financing, construction, operation, and maintenance of an onshore wind farm with a total capacity of 461MW located in Buzau County, in the Southern-East part of Romania (the Project). The Project will be implemented in two phases, i) Phase 1 with capacity of 192MW to be commissioned in early 2026, and ii) Phase 2 with capacity of 269MW to be commissioned in late 2026.
